_comment: safety batch B (evaluation & observability platforms) · langsmith · en body · verified 2026-11-06.

axes.model_access: Neither the observed nor the evaluated models come from the platform: the official product page names OpenAI, Anthropic, Vercel AI SDK, LlamaIndex and custom implementations as supported (fetched today). The evaluator surface covers human, code, LLM-as-judge, decision model and pairwise comparisons (evaluation-concepts fetched today). **Whether judge evaluators require your own model credentials is not stated on that page — recorded as unknown.**
axes.runtime: The primary form is the vendor-hosted cloud (SaaS), with BYOC and enterprise self-hosting: the official line reads that self-hosted LangSmith is an add-on to the Enterprise plan and runs in your own Kubernetes cluster, storage is bundled by default and external storage services are recommended for production (self-hosted docs fetched today). The console lives in the browser; SDKs, the CLI and the API are the code surfaces.
axes.local_files: The data plane sits on the vendor side unless you use BYOC or self-hosting; traces are reported via SDK or OpenTelemetry, with the OTLP base URL being LANGSMITH_ENDPOINT plus /otel (fetched today). The platform does not read your local codebase; **the export and deletion interface surface was not itemized today.**
axes.background: Online evaluation runs on production traces (evaluation-concepts fetched today); offline evaluation uses datasets with reference outputs for regression comparison. Today's changelog entries cover granular permissions and custom views for online evaluators. **Queue throughput, latency and sampling rules are not on record — recorded as unknown.**
axes.tools: OpenTelemetry ingestion with collector fanout to multiple destinations (fetched today); the official CLI queries and manages traces, runs, datasets, evaluators, experiments, insights and threads (fetched today); the docs index on record lists a Terraform surface that manages evaluators and rules as code. **MCP support was not verified in official statements — recorded as unknown.**
axes.context: Observed and evaluated objects are organized by workspace and project, with built-in or custom roles defined per workspace (enterprise docs fetched today); datasets carry reference outputs used for regression comparison. **Retention windows and TTL specifics were not itemized — recorded as unknown; cross-session memory is not a feature surface for this class of platform.**
axes.permissions: Compliance markers on record today: SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA and GDPR (enterprise docs direct-fetched); SAML or OIDC single sign-on with just-in-time provisioning on the same page. Tier and quota facts are a free Developer tier, Plus, and custom Enterprise including self-hosted and BYOC; price numbers are excluded per D9. **Whether customer traces train models, and the data-retention clause text, were not fetched (the privacy page returned 404 today) — recorded as unknown.**
axes.fit: Fits teams that want one console covering traces, datasets, evaluators and alerts without operating their own observability stack; applications already on OpenTelemetry can feed in first and decide later whether to fan out elsewhere. Not a fit where licensing thresholds are treated as secondary: self-hosting is, per official docs, an Enterprise add-on that also needs your own cluster and external storage. This site records which evaluation types are supported, not the scores they produce, and does not rank peers.

runs:
This site has not completed measured runs; conclusions cover the capability and license surfaces only.

**Suggested measurements** (three, each pointing at what the readable official pages do not give):

- Who owns the judge credentials: whether evaluator model calls bill to the vendor side or to your account
- End-to-end latency and miss rate of online evaluation: how long one trace takes from ingest to score
- The real operational load of self-hosting: Kubernetes cluster, external storage and license-key rotation combined
unknowns:
- Whether LLM-as-judge and decision-model evaluators require your own model credentials
- Queue throughput, latency and sampling rules for online evaluation
- Exact retention windows and TTL values
- Whether customer traces are used to train models (privacy page 404 today)
- MCP support and the outward integration surface
- The export and deletion interface inventory
- Filing-registry search
